title: Unity in Diversity, or 'Many in the One'

topics.title: Diversity of food, dress and festivals

learn.hook: Breakfast in Chennai might be idli, in Amritsar it might be paratha, and in Kolkata luchi! India is a feast of diversity.
points: India is home to many languages. The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution lists 22 languages.

Food changes with climate and crops: rice is a main food in much of the south, east and north-east, while wheat rotis are common in the north and north-west. Millets like ragi, jowar and bajra are eaten in many states.
Clothes differ too: the saree is draped in many styles, like the nine-yard nauvari of Maharashtra; Assam has the mekhela chador, Kerala the mundu, and Kashmir the warm woollen phiran.
Harvest festivals are celebrated across India with different names: Pongal in Tamil Nadu, Bihu in Assam, Lohri in Punjab and Onam in Kerala.
This variety is called diversity. It grows from differences in climate, land, history and local traditions.

example.q: Why do people in Kashmir wear a woollen phiran while people in Kerala often wear a light cotton mundu?
steps: Kashmir has very cold winters, so warm woollen clothing is needed.
Kerala is warm and humid, so light cotton clothes feel comfortable.
So clothing grows from the local climate.
example.answer: Because of the difference in climate between the two regions.

learn.reallife: Your class may have friends who speak Bengali, Tamil, Marathi or Hindi at home, and who celebrate different festivals. That's diversity in your own classroom!

items.text: The mekhela chador is worn in ___.
The warm woollen phiran is worn in ___.
The nine-yard nauvari saree comes from ___.

quiz.q: How many languages are listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution?
quiz.explain: The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution lists 22 languages.
steps: The Constitution lists languages in its Eighth Schedule.
The number listed is 22.
Answer: 22
quiz.mistake: Confuses the number of languages with the number of states

quiz.q: Pongal, a harvest festival, is mainly celebrated in which state?
quiz.explain: Pongal is the harvest festival of Tamil Nadu, named after a sweet rice dish cooked that day.
steps: Harvest festivals: Pongal (Tamil Nadu), Bihu (Assam), Lohri (Punjab), Onam (Kerala).
Answer: Tamil Nadu
quiz.mistake: Mixes up harvest festivals of different states

quiz.q: Bihu is a festival of which state?
quiz.explain: Bihu is celebrated in Assam with dance, music and feasts.
steps: From the list of harvest festivals, Bihu belongs to Assam.
Don't confuse 'Bihu' with Bihar. Answer: Assam
quiz.mistake: Links 'Bihu' with Bihar because the names sound similar

quiz.q: Which festival is linked with Kerala?
quiz.explain: Onam is Kerala's harvest festival, famous for flower rangolis (pookalam) and boat races.
steps: Onam is the harvest festival of Kerala.
Lohri is Punjab's; Bihu is Assam's.
Answer: Onam
quiz.mistake: Mixes up festivals of different states

quiz.q: Which warm, long woollen garment is worn in Kashmir?
quiz.explain: The phiran keeps people warm in Kashmir's cold winters.
steps: Kashmir has cold winters.
People there wear the warm woollen phiran.
The mundu is from Kerala; the mekhela chador from Assam. Answer: Phiran
quiz.mistake: Picks a garment from a warm region

quiz.q: What is the main reason that food differs across India?
options: People are not allowed to eat other food
Different climates and crops in different regions
All regions grow the same crops
Food is chosen by the government
quiz.explain: Each region eats what grows well in its climate and soil.
steps: Food changes with climate and crops.
Rice is common in the south and east; wheat in the north.
So the reason is different climates and crops in different regions.
Answer: Different climates and crops in different regions
quiz.mistake: Does not link food with local crops and climate

quiz.q: Which of these is a millet eaten in many parts of India?
quiz.explain: Ragi, jowar and bajra are millets; rice and wheat are other cereals.
steps: Millets eaten in many states: ragi, jowar, bajra.
Rice and wheat are other cereals; potato is a vegetable.
Answer: Ragi

quiz.q: What do we call the variety of languages, foods, clothes and festivals in India?
quiz.explain: Diversity means variety: many different ways of living side by side.
steps: Variety in languages, food, clothes and festivals.
This variety is called diversity.
Uniformity means sameness. Answer: Diversity

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'Why do people in different parts of India eat, dress and celebrate differently?'
teach.praise: Yum and wow! India's diversity in food, dress, languages and festivals grows from different climates, lands and traditions!
teach.nudge: What things are different across India, and why do you think they differ?

revise.summary: India has great diversity in languages, food, clothes and festivals. This variety grows from differences in climate, land, history and local traditions.
focus: The 22 languages of the Eighth Schedule
How climate and crops shape food: rice, wheat, millets
Regional clothes: nauvari, mekhela chador, mundu, phiran
remember: Pongal: Tamil Nadu; Bihu: Assam; Lohri: Punjab; Onam: Kerala
Phiran: Kashmir; mundu: Kerala; mekhela chador: Assam; nauvari: Maharashtra
traps: Bihu is from Assam, not Bihar
Rice and wheat are not millets
Food differs because of climate and crops, not government rules

learn.hook: Different colours of thread can be woven into one beautiful saree. India's unity is woven the same way!
points: Unity in diversity means that people with many differences also share common bonds. The chapter calls it 'many in the one'.
The Ramayana and the Mahabharata are told in many Indian languages: the Kamba Ramayanam in Tamil, the Ramcharitmanas of Tulsidas in Awadhi and the Krittivasi Ramayan in Bengali.
Many regions celebrate a new year around the middle of April with different names, such as Baisakhi, Bihu, Puthandu and Vishu.
Values like respecting elders, welcoming guests ('the guest is like god') and caring for nature are shared across regions.
The same idea can be dressed differently: the saree is one garment, but it is draped in many regional styles.

example.q: Mira in Kolkata and Kiran in Chennai both know the story of Rama, but from different books in different languages. What does this show?
steps: The story is the same at its heart.
Each region retold it in its own language and style.
So one shared story connects people across regions.
example.answer: A shared cultural thread: unity within diversity.

learn.reallife: When your school celebrates a 'Unity Day' with dances and dishes from many states, you see many colours woven into one.

games.title: Unity in diversity
items: The Ramayana has been retold in many Indian languages.
Poets in different regions wrote their own versions.
Unity in diversity means everyone must be exactly the same.
It means sharing bonds while keeping our differences.
Many states celebrate a new year around mid-April.
Baisakhi, Bihu, Puthandu and Vishu all fall around then.
The saree is draped in only one way across India.
It is draped in many regional styles.
Welcoming guests warmly is a value shared across India.
The idea 'the guest is like god' is known in many regions.

options: Sharing common bonds while having many differences
quiz.explain: Unity in diversity means we stay connected even though we are different.
steps: People in India have many differences.
They also share common bonds: 'many in the one'.
Answer: Sharing common bonds while having many differences

quiz.explain: Tulsidas wrote the Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi.
steps: The Ramcharitmanas is in Awadhi.
Its author is Tulsidas.
Kambar wrote in Tamil; Krittibas in Bengali. Answer: Tulsidas
quiz.mistake: Mixes up authors of different Ramayanas

quiz.q: The Kamba Ramayanam is written in which language?
quiz.explain: The poet Kambar wrote the Kamba Ramayanam in Tamil.
steps: The Kamba Ramayanam is the Tamil retelling.
Answer: Tamil
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the languages of different retellings

quiz.q: Which of these is a new-year festival celebrated around mid-April in Kerala?
quiz.explain: Vishu marks the new year in Kerala, around mid-April.
steps: Mid-April new-year festivals: Baisakhi, Bihu, Puthandu, Vishu.
Vishu is Kerala's.
Onam is Kerala's harvest festival, not the mid-April new year. Answer: Vishu
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Onam (harvest festival) with Vishu

quiz.q: How does the saree show 'many in the one'?
options: It is worn only in one state
One garment is draped in many regional styles
quiz.explain: The same saree is draped differently in Maharashtra, Bengal, Gujarat and elsewhere.
steps: The saree is one garment.
It is draped in many regional styles, like the nauvari of Maharashtra.
So one garment, many styles: 'many in the one'.
Answer: One garment is draped in many regional styles
quiz.mistake: Does not see the link between one item and many forms

quiz.q: Which value is shared by people across many regions of India?
quiz.explain: Treating guests with warmth is a value found across India.
steps: Shared values: respecting elders, welcoming guests, caring for nature.
'The guest is like god.'
Answer: Welcoming guests warmly
quiz.mistake: Picks an opposite of a shared value

quiz.q: Baisakhi, Bihu, Puthandu and Vishu are celebrated around the same time of year. What does this show?
options: They are the same festival in one state
Different regions share a similar celebration with different names
They are celebrated only in cities
quiz.explain: Many regions mark the new year or harvest in mid-April, each in its own style.
steps: All four come around mid-April.
Each region gives its own name and style.
So different regions share a similar celebration with different names.
Answer: Different regions share a similar celebration with different names
quiz.mistake: Does not notice the shared thread

quiz.q: Why do you think the Ramayana has been retold in so many languages?
options: People in every region wanted to enjoy it in their own language
It was banned in one language
It was written only for kings
quiz.explain: Poets made the story their own so people of their region could read and sing it.
steps: The Ramayana is told in Tamil, Awadhi, Bengali and more.
Poets retold it so people could enjoy it in their own language.
Answer: People in every region wanted to enjoy it in their own language
quiz.mistake: Gives a reason with no evidence

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'If Indians speak so many languages and eat such different foods, what holds the country together?'
teach.praise: Beautiful! Shared stories like the Ramayana, common values and festivals tie us together. That's unity in diversity, many in the one!
teach.nudge: What things do people across India share even when their languages are different?

revise.summary: Unity in diversity means people with many differences share common bonds: 'many in the one'. Shared epics, mid-April new years, common values and the saree draped in many styles show this.
focus: Meaning of unity in diversity, 'many in the one'
Ramayana in many languages and their authors
Mid-April new-year festivals with different names
remember: Kamba Ramayanam: Tamil; Ramcharitmanas (Tulsidas): Awadhi; Krittivasi Ramayan: Bengali
traps: Unity does not mean everyone must be the same
Don't link Ramcharitmanas with Tamil; it is in Awadhi
Vishu, not Onam, is Kerala's mid-April new year
